cases.customer_question: Can an RF test report be approved when version information, test evidence, and test-case documentation contain inconsistencies even though the test result is PASS?
question_variants: RF report passed but needs corrections before approval
Can a Bluetooth RF report be approved with missing log files?
How should version mismatches be handled in a test report review?
What documentation issues block RF report approval?
Is a PASS result sufficient if report evidence is incomplete?
cases.actual_issue: The RF test report contained documentation-quality issues that required correction before approval, including incorrect software version identification, missing test evidence, and inconsistent test-case notation.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Passing test results alone are not enough for a Bluetooth qualification report to be accepted. The report must accurately identify the tested software version, include all required supporting logs, and use consistent terminology throughout the document. Missing or inconsistent documentation can prevent approval even when the measured RF results pass.
cases.consultant_answer: The reviewer determined that three corrections were required before approval. The software version field needed correction because the recorded value represented firmware rather than software version information. A required log file for a 2480 MHz RF test case was missing from the shared repository. In addition, the packet-type notation in one RF test case was inconsistent with the rest of the report. The report should only proceed to approval after these issues are corrected.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification evidence must be accurate, complete, and traceable. A report cannot be considered review-ready if version identification is incorrect, mandatory supporting logs are missing, or test-case documentation is inconsistent, regardless of the overall PASS verdict.
cases.final_recommendation: Correct the software version entry, upload and verify the missing RF test log, standardize the packet-type notation across the report, and then submit the corrected report for final approval.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Incomplete or inaccurate documentation can delay report approval, require rework during review, create evidence traceability gaps, and undermine confidence that the reported test results correspond to the actual tested configuration.
